## Claims
- [source-backed] \(I_{5,4}\) is the Schur-span outside \((4^5)\), and \(A=\Lambda/I_{5,4}\) has basis \(\{\bar s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(4^5)\}\). [source-2, lines 1318-1331]
- [source-backed] For the \(5\)-Grassmannian bigrassmannian with rectangular shape \(i^j\), \(J_v\) is generated in \(\Lambda/I_{5,4}\) by \(\{\,\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(4^5)\,\}\). [source-2, lines 1354-1374]
- [proved] For \(i=j=2,\ p=2,\ c=3\), hence \(q=i+p=4,\ r=j+c=5\), one has
  \[
  J_{2,3}=\bigoplus_{(2,2)\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(4^5)}
  \mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda .
  \]
- [proved] In \(A=\Lambda/I_{5,4}\),
  \[
  A_+=(\bar h_1,\bar h_2,\bar h_3,\bar h_4).
  \]
- [proved] For every degree \(e\), all rows
  \[
  \bar h_t\bar s_\lambda
  =\sum_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq\nu\subseteq(4^5)\\
  \nu/\lambda\text{ a horizontal }t\text{-strip}}}\bar s_\nu,
  \qquad 1\le t\le4,\quad
  (2,2)\subseteq\lambda,\quad |\lambda|=e-t,
  \]
  are exactly the complete degree-\(e\) presentation of \((A_+J_{2,3})_e\).

## Strategy
Put
\[
L:=\bigoplus_{(2,2)\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(4^5)}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda
\subseteq A.
\]
The source-backed generating set gives \(J_{2,3}\subseteq L\) once \(L\) is shown to be an ideal, and gives \(L\subseteq J_{2,3}\) directly.

Indeed, for \(\mu\supseteq(2,2)\) and any Schur class \(\bar s_\eta\), the Littlewood--Richardson rule has
\[
\bar s_\eta\bar s_\mu=\sum_\rho c_{\eta,\mu}^{\rho}\bar s_\rho,
\qquad c_{\eta,\mu}^{\rho}\ne0\Rightarrow\mu\subseteq\rho.
\]
Terms with \(\rho\not\subseteq(4^5)\) vanish in \(A\); every surviving \(\rho\) therefore satisfies
\[
(2,2)\subseteq\mu\subseteq\rho\subseteq(4^5).
\]
Thus \(L\) is an ideal. Since the surviving Schur classes are a free \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(A\), the displayed sum is direct, proving the asserted formula for \(J_{2,3}\).

Since \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[h_1,h_2,\ldots]\), \(A\) is generated by the \(\bar h_t\). For \(t\ge5\),
\[
\bar h_t=\bar s_{(t)}=0,
\]
because \((t)\not\subseteq(4^5)\). Hence \(A=\mathbb Z[\bar h_1,\bar h_2,\bar h_3,\bar h_4]\), and every positive-degree polynomial belongs to their ideal. Thus
\[
A_+=(\bar h_1,\bar h_2,\bar h_3,\bar h_4).
\]

Give \(J_{2,3}\) its Schur grading. Its only nonzero degrees are \(4\le e\le20\), and
\[
(J_{2,3})_e=
\bigoplus_{\substack{(2,2)\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(4^5)\\|\lambda|=e}}
\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda;
\]
it is \(0\) for \(e<4\) or \(e>20\). Consequently,
\[
(A_+J_{2,3})_e=\sum_{t=1}^4\bar h_t(J_{2,3})_{e-t}.
\]
Applying the Pieri rule to the stated Schur bases gives precisely the listed rows. Empty source sets and empty Pieri sums contribute no rows. No \(t\ge5\) row occurs because \(\bar h_t=0\). Therefore these rows are complete degreewise presentations.

## Gaps
None for this bounded certificate. No claim is made beyond \(i=j=p=2,\ c=3\).
